subject: maths
title: Roman Numerals to 1,000 and Years
seo_title: Year 5 Roman Numerals Worksheets (to 1,000 with D and M, and Years): Free Maths Practice with Answer Key
standard_text: Read Roman numerals to 1,000 (M) and recognise years written in Roman numerals.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 Roman numerals worksheets for the National Curriculum: D and M, CD and CM, reading and writing numbers to 1,000, years like MCMXCIX and MMXXVI, film dates, foundation stones and clocks. 100 questions with answer key.
key_big: D = 500 and M = 1,000. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away: CD = 400, CM = 900.
key_sub: Partition into hundreds, tens and ones: 494 = CD + XC + IV = CDXCIV. For a year, write M for each thousand first: 1999 = M + CM + XC + IX = MCMXCIX.
body_html:
Seven symbols

In Year 4 you used I, V, X, L and C. Now add two more: D for 500 and M for 1,000.

Add or take away?

  1. Same or smaller symbol after: add. DC = 500 + 100 = 600. MD = 1,000 + 500 = 1,500.
  2. Smaller symbol before a bigger one: take it away. CD = 500 − 100 = 400. CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900.
  3. Never more than 3 of the same symbol in a row. 400 is CD, not CCCC. V, L and D are never repeated.
Take awayMeansValue
IV5 − 14
IX10 − 19
XL50 − 1040
XC100 − 1090
CD500 − 100400
CM1,000 − 100900

These six pairs are the only ones. I goes only before V or X, X only before L or C, and C only before D or M.

Read a Roman numeral

Split it into hundreds, tens and ones, then add the parts.

Read

What number is DCCXLVIII?

Hundreds: DCC = 500 + 100 + 100 = 700. Tens: XL = 50 − 10 = 40. Ones: VIII = 8. 700 + 40 + 8 = 748.

Answer: 748

Write a number as a Roman numeral

Partition the number into hundreds, tens and ones. Write each part, biggest first.

Hundreds1002003004005006007008009001,000
RomanCCCCCCCDDDCDCCDCCCCMM
Write

Write 999 in Roman numerals.

999 = 900 + 90 + 9. 900 = CM, 90 = XC and 9 = IX. Put them together.

Answer: CMXCIX (not IM)

Years in Roman numerals

Years are bigger than 1,000, but they are easy: write M for each thousand, then the rest is a number to 1,000 that you already know.

Year

Write the year 2026 in Roman numerals.

2026 = 2,000 + 20 + 6. 2,000 = MM, 20 = XX and 6 = VI.

Answer: MMXXVI

You see years like this at the end of films and TV programmes, on foundation stones of old buildings, and on monuments. Kings and queens (Henry VIII, Charles III) and clock faces use smaller Roman numerals.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
CCCC for 400, DCCCC for 900Never 4 of the same symbol in a row: CD, CM
Adding every symbol (CM = 1,100, MCM = 2,100)Smaller before bigger means take away: CM = 900, MCM = 1900
IM for 999, XD for 490, MIM for 1999Partition first: 999 = CM + XC + IX = CMXCIX
DM for 500, DD for 1,000D is never put before a bigger symbol or repeated: 500 = D, 1,000 = M
Mixing up D with L or ML = 50, D = 500, M = 1,000

faq.q: What Roman numerals do Year 5 children need to know?
faq.a: The National Curriculum in England says Year 5 pupils should read Roman numerals to 1,000 (M) and recognise years written in Roman numerals. That adds D (500) and M (1,000) to the I, V, X, L and C learned in Year 4.

faq.q: How do you write 400, 900 and 999 in Roman numerals?
faq.a: 400 is CD (500 − 100) and 900 is CM (1,000 − 100). 999 is CMXCIX (900 + 90 + 9), not IM, because I can only go before V or X.

faq.q: How do you read a year in Roman numerals, like MCMXCIX?
faq.a: Split it into parts: M = 1,000, CM = 900, XC = 90 and IX = 9. Add the parts to get 1999.

faq.q: Why are years at the end of films written in Roman numerals?
faq.a: It is a long tradition that makes the date look formal, a bit like a carved stone. You also see Roman numeral years on foundation stones, monuments and clock faces.

sets.title: The seven symbols I, V, X, L, C, D, M and numbers to 100

items.e: C = 100. C is the first letter of centum, the Latin word for a hundred (think of a century). L is 50 and D is 500.
D = 500. Do not mix it up with L (50) or M (1,000).
M = 1,000. It comes from mille, the Latin word for a thousand. M does not stand for a million.
L = 50. D is 500, C is 100 and V is 5.
500 has its own symbol: D. DM is not allowed: D is never put before a bigger symbol. CCCCC uses 5 Cs, but you never write more than 3 of the same symbol in a row. M is 1,000.
1,000 has its own symbol: M. DD is not allowed: D is never repeated. D is 500 and CM is 900.
C = 100. L is 50, D is 500 and XC is 90.

items.q: Which three symbols are never repeated, like VV or DD?
items.e: V, L and D are never repeated, because two of them make another symbol: VV = X, LL = C and DD = M.

items.q: Which symbols can go in front of a bigger symbol to be taken away?
items.e: Only I, X and C are taken away: IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM. V, L and D are never put before a bigger symbol.

items.q: What is the most times you can write the same symbol in a row?
items.e: Never more than 3 in a row: III = 3, XXX = 30, CCC = 300. 4 is IV, 40 is XL and 400 is CD.
Split it: X = 10; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XIV = 10 + 4 = 14. The I is before the V, so take it away: XIV is not 16.
Split it: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XXXIX = 30 + 9 = 39. IX is 9, not 11, so XXXIX is not 41.
Split it: XL = 50 − 10 = 40; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XLIX = 40 + 9 = 49. Adding every symbol gives 71, which is wrong.
Split it: LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80; VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So LXXXVIII = 80 + 8 = 88. Count carefully: L and three Xs make 80, then VIII is 8.
Split it: XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XCIV = 90 + 4 = 94. XC is 90, not 110, and IV is 4, not 6.
XL = 50 − 10 = 40, so 40 = XL. XXXX is wrong: never 4 Xs in a row. LX is 60.
Partition 64 into 60 + 4. 60 = LX and 4 = IV. So 64 = LXIV. IV is 4, so LXVI (66) is wrong, and IIII is never used.
XC = 100 − 10 = 90, so 90 = XC. CX is 110: the smaller symbol must come before the bigger one to take away.
Partition 49 into 40 + 9. 40 = XL and 9 = IX. So 49 = XLIX. IL is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.
Partition 99 into 90 + 9. 90 = XC and 9 = IX. So 99 = XCIX. IC is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

sets.title: Read Roman numerals to 1,000: CD, D, DC, CM and M

items.e: CCC = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300. Each C is 100. Do not mix C up with X (10).
DC = 500 + 100 = 600. The smaller C comes after the D, so add it. D is 500, not 1,000 (M) or 50 (L).
CD = 500 − 100 = 400. The smaller C comes before the D, so take it away: CD is not 600.
CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900. The C comes before the M, so take it away: CM is not 1,100.
DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800. Count the Cs: there are three. D is 500, not 1,000.
Split it: C = 100; XX = 10 + 10 = 20. So CXX = 100 + 20 = 120. The Xs come after the C, so add them. Roman numerals have no place value, so it is not 102.
Split it: CC = 100 + 100 = 200; LX = 50 + 10 = 60. So CCLX = 200 + 60 = 260. LX is 60. XL would be 40.
Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; L = 50. So CDL = 400 + 50 = 450. CD is 400, not 600, so CDL is not 650.
Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CDIX = 400 + 9 = 409. CD is 400 and IX is 9: take away both times.
Split it: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So CMIV = 900 + 4 = 904. CM is 900 and IV is 4: take away both times.
Split it: C = 100; XL = 50 − 10 = 40; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CXLIX = 100 + 40 + 9 = 149. XL is 40, not 60, and IX is 9, not 11.

Split it: DC = 500 + 100 = 600; LX = 50 + 10 = 60; VI = 5 + 1 = 6. So DCLXVI = 600 + 60 + 6 = 666. Every symbol here is followed by a smaller one, so add them all. DCLXVI uses D, C, L, X, V and I once each.
Split it: DCC = 500 + 100 + 100 = 700; LXX = 50 + 10 + 10 = 70; VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So DCCLXXVII = 700 + 70 + 7 = 777. Count carefully: DCC = 700, LXX = 70, VII = 7.
Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So CDXCIV = 400 + 90 + 4 = 494. CD is 400 (not 600), XC is 90 (not 110) and IV is 4 (not 6).
Split it: DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800; LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80; VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So DCCCLXXXVIII = 800 + 80 + 8 = 888. Count carefully: three Cs, three Xs and three Is.
Split it: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900; XC = 100 − 10 = 90; IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So CMXCIX = 900 + 90 + 9 = 999. 999 is the biggest number below 1,000. It is never written IM.

sets.title: Write numbers to 1,000 in Roman numerals

items.e: Partition 140 into 100 + 40. 100 = C and 40 = XL. So 140 = CXL. Write the hundreds first, then the tens: C then XL.
CD = 500 − 100 = 400, so 400 = CD. CCCC is wrong (never 4 Cs in a row) and DC is 600. Only one C can go before D.
DC = 500 + 100 = 600, so 600 = DC. The C comes after the D because we add it. CD would be 400.
Partition 250 into 200 + 50. 200 = CC and 50 = L. So 250 = CCL. Write the bigger values first. L is never repeated, so CLL is wrong.
760 = 700 + 60. DCC = 700, so the missing part is 60 = LX.
CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900, so 900 = CM. DCCCC has 4 Cs in a row, and MC is 1,100.
Partition 444 into 400 + 40 + 4. 400 = CD, 40 = XL and 4 = IV. So 444 = CDXLIV. Take away in every part: CD, XL, IV. Swapping them all gives DCLXVI, which is 666.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: CCCC is not correct: 400 is written CD. The others are correct: CD = 400, DC = 600, CM = 900.
Partition 490 into 400 + 90. 400 = CD and 90 = XC. So 490 = CDXC. XD is not allowed: X can only go before L or C.
Partition 495 into 400 + 90 + 5. 400 = CD, 90 = XC and 5 = V. So 495 = CDXCV. VD is not allowed: V is never put before a bigger symbol. CDXCIV is 494.
Partition 499 into 400 + 90 + 9. 400 = CD, 90 = XC and 9 = IX. So 499 = CDXCIX. ID and IC are not allowed: I can only go before V or X.
Partition 550 into 500 + 50. 500 = D and 50 = L. So 550 = DL. LD is not allowed: L is never put before a bigger symbol. DXL is 540.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: XD is not correct: X can only go before L or C, so 490 = CD + XC = CDXC. The others are correct: CDXC = 490, CMXL = 940, DXC = 590.
Partition 707 into 700 + 7. 700 = DCC and 7 = VII. So 707 = DCCVII. There are no tens, so write nothing for them. DCCLXX is 770.
940 = 900 + 40. CM = 900, so the missing part is 40 = XL.
Partition 840 into 800 + 40. 800 = DCCC and 40 = XL. So 840 = DCCCXL. 800 is DCCC: only one C can go before M, so CCM is wrong.
Partition 385 into 300 + 80 + 5. 300 = CCC, 80 = LXXX and 5 = V. So 385 = CCCLXXXV. 80 = LXXX. Only one X can go before C, so XXC is wrong.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: DD is not correct: D is never repeated, so 1,000 is written M. The others are correct: M = 1,000, CC = 200, CCC = 300.
Partition 990 into 900 + 90. 900 = CM and 90 = XC. So 990 = CMXC. XM is not allowed: X can only go before L or C.
Partition 999 into 900 + 90 + 9. 900 = CM, 90 = XC and 9 = IX. So 999 = CMXCIX. IM is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

sets.title: Years in Roman numerals: MCM, MCMXCIX and MMXXVI

items.e: Split it: MM = 1,000 + 1,000 = 2,000; V = 5. So MMV = 2,000 + 5. The year is 2005. Count both Ms. V is 5: do not mix it up with L (50) or X (10).
Split it: MM = 1,000 + 1,000 = 2,000; X = 10. So MMX = 2,000 + 10. The year is 2010. Count both Ms. X is 10, not 100.
Split it: M = 1,000; DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800. So MDCCC = 1,000 + 800. The year is 1800. Count the Cs: three. D is 500, not 50.
Split it: M = 1,000; CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900. So MCM = 1,000 + 900. The year is 1900. The C is before the second M, so take it away: CM = 900. MCM is not 2100.
Split it: M = 1,000; DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800; L = 50. So MDCCCL = 1,000 + 800 + 50. The year is 1850. Do not forget the L at the end.
Split it: M = 1,000; LX = 50 + 10 = 60; VI = 5 + 1 = 6. So MLXVI = 1,000 + 60 + 6. The year is 1066. LX is 60 and VI is 6. This is the year of the Battle of Hastings.
Split it: MM = 1,000 + 1,000 = 2,000; X = 10; II = 1 + 1 = 2. So MMXII = 2,000 + 10 + 2. The year is 2012. Count both Ms, then read XII = 12.
Split it: M = 1,000; DC = 500 + 100 = 600; LX = 50 + 10 = 60; VI = 5 + 1 = 6. So MDCLXVI = 1,000 + 600 + 60 + 6. The year is 1666. This is the year of the Great Fire of London.

items.q: Write the year 1500 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 1500 into 1,000 + 500. 1,000 = M and 500 = D. So 1500 = MD. Write the thousands first: M, then D. DM is not allowed: D is never put before a bigger symbol.

items.q: Write the year 1950 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 1950 into 1,000 + 900 + 50. 1,000 = M, 900 = CM and 50 = L. So 1950 = MCML. MLM is not allowed: L is never put before a bigger symbol.

items.q: Write the year 1984 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 1984 into 1,000 + 900 + 80 + 4. 1,000 = M, 900 = CM, 80 = LXXX and 4 = IV. So 1984 = MCMLXXXIV. IV is 4. VI would be 6.

items.q: Write the year 1999 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 1999 into 1,000 + 900 + 90 + 9. 1,000 = M, 900 = CM, 90 = XC and 9 = IX. So 1999 = MCMXCIX. MIM is a common mistake: I can only go before V or X, so 999 must be CMXCIX.

items.q: Write the year 2020 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 2020 into 2,000 + 20. 2,000 = MM and 20 = XX. So 2020 = MMXX. 2,000 needs two Ms: MXX is 1020.

items.q: Write the year 2026 in Roman numerals.
items.e: Partition 2026 into 2,000 + 20 + 6. 2,000 = MM, 20 = XX and 6 = VI. So 2026 = MMXXVI. VI is 6 (V then I). IV would be 4, and V is never repeated.
MCMXL = 1940, MCMLXVI = 1966, MCMLXXX = 1980, MCMXCIX = 1999. MCMXL is the earliest year.
MCMLXXXVIII = 1988, MCMXCIX = 1999, MMI = 2001, MMX = 2010. MMX is the latest. A longer numeral is not always a bigger number.

sets.title: Real life: films, foundation stones, kings and queens, and calculations

items.e: The minute hand (red) points to III, which is quarter past. The hour hand has just passed X (10), so it is quarter past ten. Be careful: X is 10 and XI is 11.
The minute hand (red) points to IX, which is quarter to. The hour hand is nearly at IV (4), so it is quarter to four. Be careful: IV is 4, not 6.

items.q: At the end of a film, Mohammed sees “© MCMXCVII”. In what year was the film made?
In what year was this stone laid?
Queen Victoria became queen in MDCCCXXXVII. What year was that?
items.e: Split it: M = 1,000; DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800; XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30; VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So MDCCCXXXVII = 1,000 + 800 + 30 + 7. The year is 1837. Count the Cs (three) and the Xs (three). VII is 7.

items.q: Queen Elizabeth II was crowned in MCMLIII. What year was that?
items.e: Split it: M = 1,000; CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900; L = 50; III = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. So MCMLIII = 1,000 + 900 + 50 + 3. The year is 1953. L is 50 and III is 3.

items.q: A monument says MDCCCXV, the year of the Battle of Waterloo. What year is that?
The London 2012 Olympic Games were called “the Games of the XXX Olympiad”. Which Olympiad was that?
items.e: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30, so London 2012 was the 30th Olympiad. X is 10, not 1 or 100.

items.q: Grace’s favourite film came out in MCMXCIX and its sequel in MMIX. How many years apart are they?
items.e: MCMXCIX = 1999 and MMIX = 2009. 2009 − 1999 = 10 years. Reading IX as 11 gives 12 or 8, and forgetting the first M of MCMXCIX gives 1,010.

items.q: M comes from mille, the Latin word for a thousand. Which English word also comes from mille?
items.e: A millennium is 1,000 years. Metre, minute and medium come from other Latin and Greek words.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: DCCCLXXX = 880, DCCCXC = 890, CM = 900, CMX = 910. CMX is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which list of years goes from earliest to latest?
items.e: MCMLX = 1960, MCMLXX = 1970, MCMXC = 1990. From earliest to latest: MCMLX, MCMLXX, MCMXC.

items.q: Work out CM + C. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CM = 900 and C = 100. 900 + 100 = 1,000, and 1,000 = M. CMC just puts the numerals side by side. DD is not allowed: D is never repeated.

items.q: Work out M − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: M = 1,000 and I = 1. 1,000 − 1 = 999, and 999 = CMXCIX. IM is not allowed: I can only go before V or X. MI is 1,001.

items.q: Work out D − CC. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: D = 500 and CC = 200. 500 − 200 = 300, and 300 = CCC. CCD is not a Roman numeral: only one C can go before D. DCC is 500 + 200.

items.q: Work out CDL + L. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CDL = 450 and L = 50. 450 + 50 = 500, and 500 = D. CD is 400, not 600, so the answer is not DCC (700).

items.q: Work out C × V. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and V = 5. 100 × 5 = 500, and 500 = D. CV is 105, not 100 × 5. M is 100 × 10. CCCCC has too many Cs.

items.q: A foundation stone says MCMXXXVI. Charlie reads it as 2136. What mistake did he make?
c: Added the C instead of taking it away
items.e: MCMXXXVI = M + CM + XXX + VI = 1,000 + 900 + 30 + 6, so the year is 1936. Adding the C gives 1,000 + 100 + 1,000 + 30 + 6 = 2136. The C comes before the M, so it must be taken away.
MIM is not correct: I can only go before V or X. 1999 is written MCMXCIX. The others are correct: MCMXCIX = 1999, MCMLXXX = 1980, MMXX = 2020.
